output.title: Expected wait time for a member callback
output.draft_text:
Question: How long does a member usually wait for a callback?

Answer: When a member requests a callback, they can usually expect to hear back within [standard callback timeframe, e.g., number of business hours or days]. Callbacks are made during [callback hours of operation and time zone]. If the request is submitted [after hours / on a weekend / on a holiday], the timeframe starts on [when the clock starts, e.g., the next business day].

Callback timing may be different for [request types or priority levels with different timeframes, e.g., urgent clinical or pharmacy issues], which are returned within [priority callback timeframe].

When the callback is made, we will call the member at [phone number used, e.g., the number on file or the number given in the request]. If the member does not answer, we will [number of attempts and voicemail practice].

If the member has not received a callback within [timeframe after which the member should follow up], the advocate should [escalation or follow-up step, e.g., check the request status in system name, resubmit, or escalate to team]. Let the member know they can also reach us at [alternate contact phone number or channel] during [hours].

Advocate tip: Tell the member the expected timeframe when the callback is requested and confirm the best phone number to reach them.
placeholders: [standard callback timeframe, e.g., number of business hours or days]
[callback hours of operation and time zone]
[after hours / on a weekend / on a holiday]
[when the clock starts, e.g., the next business day]
[request types or priority levels with different timeframes, e.g., urgent clinical or pharmacy issues]
[phone number used, e.g., the number on file or the number given in the request]
[timeframe after which the member should follow up]
[escalation or follow-up step, e.g., check the request status in system name, resubmit, or escalate to team]
author_checklist: Confirm the standard callback timeframe, and whether it is measured in business or calendar time.
Confirm callback hours of operation and the time zone used.
Confirm how requests made after hours, on weekends, or on holidays are handled and when the timeframe starts.
Confirm whether some request types (for example, urgent, clinical, or pharmacy) have a different or priority callback timeframe.
Confirm which phone number is used for callbacks, how many attempts are made, and whether a voicemail is left.
Confirm the follow-up or escalation step and the system or team involved when a callback is missed.
Confirm the alternate contact number or channel and its hours.
Confirm whether this answer applies to all lines of business or needs separate versions, which determines the correct knowledge base.
Confirm whether any contractual, regulatory, or service-level commitments govern callback timing and must be cited or reviewed by legal or compliance.
Remove any placeholder sections that do not apply before approval.
